attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The bridge is valid, but no explicit target-clean G_N,A_N is known with a provable unrestricted circuit lower bound SIZE(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon}. A proof of that source bound must also avoid natural-proof density, relativizing oracle, and advice-leakage obstructions.
steps: Fix constants d>1, q, rho, epsilon with max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, and define H_N by a target-clean generated OR or more general consumer over M=N^q length-L SAT instances.
Assume toward contradiction that SAT is in P/poly, so for some c every sufficiently large length l has SAT circuits C_l of size O(l^c).
For each valid N, copy C_{L(N)} into every generated target slot and wire these copies to A_N; the generator/consumer contributes N^rho gates and the target copies contribute N^q L^c gates.
Since L=(log N)^d, the copy cost is N^{q+o(1)} for fixed c,d. Hence SIZE(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}.
Choose delta>0 with max{rho,q}+delta<1+epsilon. For all large valid N the composed circuit has size below N^{1+epsilon}, contradicting the i.o. source lower bound.
Audit the unconditional falsifier: replacing each SAT call by exhaustive search costs N^rho+N^q2^L poly(L), which is N^{q+omega(1)} for d>1, so it does not itself refute an N^{1+epsilon} lower bound.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is route-level progress only. It shows that one sharply specified weak lower bound would imply SAT notin P/poly; it does not supply the weak lower bound or a non-natural method for proving it.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: polylog generated-OR carrier

assumptions: q,rho,d,epsilon are constants with d>1 and max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
G_N(x,i) outputs a valid SAT instance of length L(N), or a fixed padded unsatisfiable instance on malformed indices.
A_N is deterministic and target-clean; it does not contain the SAT truth table, a hardwired satisfying assignment table, or advice depending on the hypothetical SAT circuit.
The source lower bound is against unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits for the length-N truth table of H_N.
SAT in P/poly means there is a fixed c such that SAT on all sufficiently large input lengths has circuits of size O(n^c).
definitions: source object: H_N^{G,A}(x)=A_N(x, SAT_L(G_N(x,1)),...,SAT_L(G_N(x,M))) for x in {0,1}^N, where M=N^q and L=(log N)^d.
target object: nonuniform Boolean circuits for SAT on length-L encodings, with target consequence SAT notin P/poly and therefore NP not subset P/poly.
controlled interface: G_N and A_N are uniform or explicitly constructible circuits of total size at most N^rho and use only generated formula bits plus SAT answers.
target-preserving condition: for some epsilon>0, max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, no SAT-dependent advice is embedded, and the source lower bound holds on infinitely many valid lengths.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Conditional bridge lemma: it turns a barely-superlinear lower bound for one generated-SAT carrier into a nonuniform SAT lower bound for every polynomial exponent.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let L(N)=(log N)^d with fixed d>1, M(N)=N^q, and let a target-clean generator/consumer pair (G_N,A_N) of circuit size at most N^rho define H_N by consuming M generated SAT instances of length L. If max{rho,q}<1+epsilon and SIZE(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} for infinitely many valid N, then SAT has no polynomial-size nonuniform circuits; hence NP is not contained in P/poly.

assumptions: The generator and consumer cost N^rho is counted in the upper bound.

The source lower bound is asserted against unrestricted deterministic circuits, so unconditional deterministic lookup is a valid falsifier.

Let lambda be the exponent satisfying L(N)=lambda log_2 N+O(log log N), when such a constant exists.
Lookup-safe means the unconditional brute-force upper bound is not already below the asserted source lower-bound threshold.

candidate_lemmas.statement: For generated-SAT carriers, brute-force replacement of SAT gives an unconditional lookup upper bound. Thus a proposed source lower bound SIZE(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} is falsified whenever N^rho+N^q 2^{L(N)} poly(L(N)) is below N^{1+epsilon} infinitely often. The superlogarithmic polylog choice L=(log N)^d with d>1 avoids this particular falsifier.

assumptions: The target consequence is SAT notin P/poly, not merely hardness of a bespoke nonuniform language.

definitions: Advice leakage is any nonuniform string or circuit fragment not charged to N^rho and correlated with SAT on length L(N).
Target-clean substitution means the only use of the hypothetical SAT circuit is through explicit copies wired into generated query positions.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation does not rule out a(N)=omega(log N) witnesses, nonblack-box syntax checks, or proof objects whose usefulness is not universal over all witnesses.
steps: Start with a claimed lower-bound route: a deterministic verifier V reads a small number q of locations of a candidate truth table y and accepts SAT_n with some witness w while rejecting all n^k-size circuit truth tables for every witness.
Define the induced property P_N by existentially quantifying over witnesses.
Constructivity: decide P_N by enumerating all 2^a witnesses and simulating V; this is poly(N) when a=O(log N).
Largeness: fix the accepting witness w* for SAT_n and the accepting adaptive transcript. Every table agreeing with the transcript on its queried bits is accepted, giving density at least 2^{-q}.
Usefulness: universal soundness over all witnesses implies no n^k-size circuit truth table lies in P_N.
Therefore a short-witness, logarithmic-query Merlin-local SAT separator is a standard natural property and is blocked by the natural-proof falsifier under strong PRFs.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This only classifies a route object against a barrier. It gives no lower bound for SAT and does not decide P versus NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: Merlin-Local Naturalization Gate

assumptions: Completeness: there exists w* with V^{SAT_n}(1^N,w*)=1.
Usefulness soundness: for every circuit C of size at most n^k and every witness w, V^{tt(C)}(1^N,w)=0.
The verifier is deterministic after the witness is fixed; randomized variants require the seed-elimination audit from the previous cycle.
Witness enumeration is allowed in the constructivity budget only when 2^{a(N)} poly(N) is polynomial in N.
definitions: source object: a deterministic Merlin-local separator V for the SAT_n truth table y in {0,1}^N, N=2^n, with witness length a(N), adaptive query bound q(N), and poly(N)-time query computation.
target object: a Razborov-Rudich natural property P_N of N-bit truth tables that is constructive in poly(N), has density at least 1/poly(N), and is useful against SIZE(n^k).
controlled interface: define P_N={y in {0,1}^N : exists w in {0,1}^{a(N)} such that V^y(1^N,w)=1}, and transfer separator soundness into usefulness.
target-preserving condition: V accepts SAT_n for some witness, rejects every truth table computed by every n^k-size circuit for every witness, and has a(N)=O(log N) and q(N)=O(log N).
adaptive queries are allowed; after fixing the accepting witness and transcript, the accepted inputs contain one cylinder fixing at most q(N) truth-table positions.
the natural-proof obstruction is invoked only under the standard strong PRF hypothesis; without that hypothesis the lemma is a barrier audit, not a P != NP theorem.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known sparse global invariant proves high general circuit complexity for a 2^{O(m)}-streamed table while also proving that all subthreshold block-seek implementations are impossible.
steps: Model a candidate non-enumerative repair as a checkpointed sequential decompressor: certificate p has length O(m), V streams T_p in 2^{c m}, and a resume circuit A_{m,p} outputs any block of length L=2^{beta m}.
Fix an accepted p and construct a circuit for f_p(x): compute the block index of x, invoke A_{m,p}, and select the bit of x inside that block.
The resulting circuit size is at most 2^{max{beta,sigma}m+o(m)}, where 2^{sigma m} bounds the resume circuit.
If max{beta,sigma}<epsilon, this contradicts MCSP_m(T_p)>2^{epsilon m}; therefore fine-grained checkpointing, bit generators, and local transcript proof systems are invalid source implementations.
Setting beta>=epsilon avoids immediate leakage but destroys the hoped-for local verification advantage; soundness still needs a global non-enumerative invariant.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a route-level falsifier for localizable certificate sources and protects the valid carrier bridge; it does not construct the required MCSP no-side carrier or prove P != NP.

assumptions: For every accepted p, the verifier outputs a full truth table T_p of an m-input Boolean function f_p.
No-side soundness claims MCSP_m(T_p)>2^{epsilon m} for every accepted p.
A block-seek implementation may depend on the fixed certificate p but not on additional nonuniform advice beyond the circuit A_{m,p}.
The within-block bit position can be selected by hardwiring or a multiplexer of size O(2^{beta m} poly(m)).
definitions: source object: an O(m)-bit sequential MCSP no-side certificate p whose verifier streams T_p in {0,1}^{2^m} within 2^{c m} time.
target object: an E-uniform truth-table family yielding SIZE(2^{delta n}) lower bounds on all sufficiently large input lengths after the carrier extraction.
controlled interface: block-seek access to a certified stream is modeled by circuits A_{m,p} of size 2^{sigma m} outputting blocks of length 2^{beta m}.
target-preserving condition: the transfer is valid only when no accepted certificate admits subthreshold block access with max{beta,sigma}<epsilon, and the certified lengths remain kappa-dense.

held_fixed_controls: No-side threshold MCSP_m(T_p)>2^{epsilon m} for fixed epsilon>0.
Certificate length O(m) and total streaming verification time 2^{O(m)}.
No nonuniform advice beyond the certificate p.
Kappa-dense source lengths for the extraction target.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch is blocked at source construction, not extraction. Varying the block-seek exponent beta directly tests whether checkpointed or decompressor-style certificates are target-preserving or leak small circuits.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: An O(m)-bit certificate p for an m-input MCSP no-side truth table T_p is verified by a 2^{c m}-time streaming decompressor V. Add optional checkpoints every L=2^{beta m} output bits, with a uniform resume/block circuit R_{m,p} of size 2^{sigma m}.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal block-to-bit circuit simulation plus a density-preserving carrier extraction showing that sequential explicitness is sufficient for E search, while random access, block access, and advice are excluded from the target-preserving interface.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: The block length exponent beta, with sigma treated as the candidate resume-access exponent and epsilon held as the MCSP threshold.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 14 adds an exact locality threshold: any accepted certificate with block access below exponent epsilon yields small circuits for its own table, so it cannot be a sound MCSP no-side carrier. The valid bridge survives, but the remaining source must be sparse, non-enumerative, non-natural in the large-property sense, nonuniform-free, and globally sequential with seek cost at least 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}.
